modern: As physicians always have their instruments and knives ready for cases which suddenly require their skill, so you should have principles ready for understanding things divine and human, and for doing everything, even the smallest thing, with a remembrance of the bond which unites the divine and the human to one another. For you will not do anything well which concerns man without at the same time referring it to things divine; nor the reverse.
original: As physicians have always their instruments and knives ready for cases which suddenly require their skill, so do thou have principles ready for the understanding of things divine and human, and for doing everything, even the smallest, with a recollection of the bond which unites the divine and human to one another. For neither wilt thou do anything well which pertains to man without at the same time having a reference to things divine; nor the contrary.
